message.content:
Below is a concise summary of key tenant‑rights and responsibilities under Texas law (as of May 2026). It’s meant as a quick reference—if you have a particular situation (e.g., eviction notice, repair dispute), consult your local housing agency or attorney for tailored advice. | Area | What You’re Generally Allowed / Required | |------|------------------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent if lease says so.
• Must return deposit within 30 days after tenancy ends unless landlord lists unpaid amounts (rent, damages) and provides itemized statement. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlords must keep premises safe, sanitary, structurally sound, and compliant with building codes.
• If repairs aren’t made promptly, tenants can file a complaint with the county health department or take “repair‑and‑deduct” action (pay for needed work themselves and deduct cost from rent). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent due dates set in lease; late fees allowed only if specified in lease and reasonable.
• Tenants cannot refuse to pay rent because they disagree with a clause in the lease. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord needs written notice at least 24 hours before entry, except emergencies.
• Notice must specify purpose and time. | | **Eviction Process** | • Evictions require proper notice (usually 3–30 days depending on reason).
• Courts will consider whether landlord followed correct procedure and complied with habitability standards. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a fixed‑term lease early only if both agree or if there’s a breach by the other side.
• For month‑to‑month leases, either party gives 30‑day written notice. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, etc. | | **Privacy** | • Tenant has right to privacy; landlords cannot conduct surveillance without consent. | ### Quick Tips 1. **Document Everything:** Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of damage, and maintenance requests. 2. **Know Your Lease Terms:** Some clauses might waive certain rights (like requiring a longer security deposit); read carefully. 3. **Use Local Resources:** County clerk offices often handle small claims related to deposits or minor disputes. If you encounter a problem (unlawful eviction notice, unreturned deposit, unsafe living conditions), contact: * **County Clerk/Justice Court** – for filing complaints or small‑claims actions. * **Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)** – for licensing issues. * **Local Legal Aid Organizations** – many offer free consultations for low‑income residents. Feel free to ask more specifics!
